newsitem.title: UK: Investors eye MFI windfall boost.
newsitem.headline: Investors eye MFI windfall boost.

text.p: Investors will be looking for hints that MFI Furniture Group Plc is capturing some of the windfall cash from building society flotations when Britain's biggest fitted kitchens and furniture retailer reports annual results next Tuesday.
MFI is set to increase pre-tax profits by about 23 percent for the year to end April 1997, but is likely to have encountered much tougher trading in the second half.

In March, after its key winter sale, MFI reported an unexpected slowdown in second half sales. Analysts now hope the recovery in the housing market plus extra cash hitting shoppers' pockets from the demutualisation of home loan groups like Halifax and Alliance and Leicester may have revived sales in recent weeks.
"The key is current trading," said one retail analyst, "sales have slowed over the past 12 months as comparisons have got tougher, hopefully this will be offset by windfall spending." he said.
There are expectations that MFI will also benefit as the housing market recovery spreads beyond the south east of England, where it has been concentrated.

Analysts also want an update on whether the new-look MFI stores - MFI Homeworks - are continuing to outperform the rest of the chain. In the first half these stores, which carry a wider range of goods, produced a double figure sales uplift.
But the strong pound is likely to have affected earnings from MFI's stores in France, which trade under the Hygena brand name, analysts said.
Pre-tax profits are expected to rise to between 70 and 74.5 million stg from 58.1 million in the previous year. Analysts predict a dividend of about 4.6 to 5.0 pence, up from 4.4 pence.

The shares, which fell sharply in March on news of the sales slowdown, have dropped back further since then. One analyst said the stock looked cheap and recommended it as a buy, but another preferred a hold due to uncertainty about interest rates and potential tax rises in the Labour government's first budget next Wednesday.
The shares were at 134p, up 1p by 0911 GMT.
